Standard calculation with Annual payment frequency (Multiplier: 1)
Payment frequency supplied in all lowercase letters

Payment frequency supplied in UPPERCASE letters to the test harness. NOTE: this does NOT genuinely exercise R2 case-insensitivity in the application. The calculator's <select> only ever submits a fixed lowercase value attribute regardless of which option's visible text is matched, so the real app never receives an uppercase frequency string here. This case only proves the Selenium POM can select the right dropdown option when given mixed-case test input. True R2 coverage for this app comes only from the Members table (see MembersValidationTest, member M004) where raw mixed-case strings reach the app's lookup logic directly, and from ApplicationCoreLogicTest which calls the app's own annualFor() function directly via JavaScript to bypass this UI constraint.
ruleReference: R1 (dropdown-selection robustness only — NOT a genuine R2 case-insensitivity test; see description)

description: Amount expressed as a hexadecimal literal. JS Number('0x10') parses this to 16 (not NaN), so the app's isNaN-based check does not reject it, while Java's BigDecimal does not support hex notation and throws. This test documents a genuine app-vs-spec mismatch (see BUG_REPORTS.md Finding F1) rather than asserting a fabricated requirement.
ruleReference: R8 (ambiguous): a hex literal is not a normal monetary numeric input; see BUG_REPORTS.md Finding F1 for the full analysis of this expected FAIL.
